newsitem.title: GERMANY: Meister-investors not shunning mark amid EMU fears.
newsitem.headline: Meister-investors not shunning mark amid EMU fears.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister said on Monday that empirical data suggested investors were not shifting funds out of the mark because of fears relating to Europe's planned monetary union.

"Some assume that Eurosceptical investors will avoid the mark in the run-up to monetary union, or perhaps have been doing so for some time, and shift their portfolios into other currencies like the U.S. dollar, British pound or Swiss franc," Meister said according to the text of a speech to be held in Buenos Aires.
"But all data so far on the currency structure of international investments -- interpreted with all due caution -- speak against this theory of an 'exit out of the mark.'
"The interest rate and exchange rate constellation too do not suggest a fundamentally different assessment in the slightly longer term."
The Bundesbank made a text of the speech to the Argentine banking association ADEBA available ahead of delivery.
Meister said it was hard to predict the extent to which investors after monetary union will keep their previous mark-denominated holdings in Euros.
"Theoretical considerations about portfolios suggest a diversification of currency investments, which would open up additional chances for the Euro," Meister said.
Meister said it was equally hard to predict how the Euro will affect the role of the dollar and the Japanese yen as reserve currencies.
The Euro's status as an investment and reserve currency will also determine its role as a transaction currency, Meister said.
He noted that after monetary union Europe will have one of the world's largest financial markets.

"With a stable Euro Europe as a financial centre can enter into direct competition with the world's other great financial markets, especially the U.S. financial market and the U.S. dollar," Meister said.
"The appearance of the Euro will trigger a new competition among the world's main currencies, whether this is wanted or not." --David Crossland, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
